To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

LH4, which was designed as a novel monofunctional anticancer drug, is more active in resistant cell lines than cisplatin, and synergism from LH4 in combination with phytochemical anticancer agents is observed in resistant cell lines, but not in the sensitive parent line.

LH4 was found more active against the cisplatin-resistant A2780(c) cell line than the parent A 2780 cell line and that bolus administration was the most synergistic sequence in both the parent and resistant cell lines.
LH4 is a more active drug than cisplatin against cisplatin-resistant human ovarian cancer cell models and combinations of LH4, cisplatin and phytochemicals are synergistic in activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of novel platinum anticancer drugs that have improved efficacy against platinum-resistant tumors and the development of novel combinations with phytochemcials for improved anticancer activity.
the development of novel platinum-based drugs that have activity against cisplatin-resistant tumor models and the design of combinations that have synergistic activity against these tumor models.
the design, synthesis and biological evaluation of a new series of monofunctionational platinum compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synergism in activity of LH4 from its combination with phytochemical capsaicin and cisplatin is dependent on the sequence of administration.

the LH4/cisplatin combination is more active than the cisplatin monotherapy in the cisplatin sensitive A2780 and more active than cisplatin monotheraphy in the resistant cell lines A2780(cispR), A2780(Zd0473R) and OVCAR-3.
the monofunctional LH4 is a novel anticancer drug with potential for further development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the monofunctional LH4 is a novel platinum compound which exhibits greater activity than cisplatin against cisplatin-resistant tumor models and synergistically combines with phytochemical agents to produce greater activity.
monofunctional LH4, which is more active than cisplatin, is a potential anticancer drug.
the monofunctional tris(benzimadazole)platinum(II) complex LH4 has the potential to be a new anticancer drug for the treatment of ovarian cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of LH4 with the phytochemicals, capsaicin and curcumin is synergistic in ovarian cancer cells.

the monofunctional LH4 compound is more active against resistant tumor cells than cisplatin and that combinations of LH4 and phytochemicals are more synergistic than the combinations of cisplatin and phytochemical.
the combination of LH4 with capsaicins, curcumins, and quercetin is more effective against cisplatin resistant ovarian tumor models than cisplatin itself.
